subject: maths
title: Factors, Multiples and Prime Numbers
seo_title: Year 5 Factors, Multiples and Primes Worksheets: Factor Pairs, Prime, Square and Cube Numbers
standard_text: Identify multiples and factors, including finding all factor pairs of a number, and common factors of two numbers; know and use the vocabulary of prime numbers, prime factors and composite (non-prime) numbers; establish whether a number up to 100 is prime and recall prime numbers up to 19; recognise and use square numbers and cube numbers, and the notation for squared (²) and cubed (³).
meta_desc: Free Year 5 maths worksheets on factors, multiples and prime numbers: factor pairs, common factors, prime and composite numbers, prime factors, square numbers and cube numbers. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: A factor divides a number exactly; a multiple is in its times table. A prime number has exactly two factors.
key_sub: 1 is not prime, and 2 is the only even prime. Learn the primes to 19: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. 7² = 7 × 7 = 49 and 3³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
body_html:
Factors and factor pairs

A factor divides a number exactly, with no remainder. Factors come in pairs that multiply to make the number. 3 × 4 = 12, so 3 and 4 are a factor pair of 12.

To find all the factors, test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. Stop when the pairs meet.

Example

Find all the factors of 30.

1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. 4 does not divide 30. The next number, 6, is already in a pair, so stop.

Answer: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30

Multiples and common factors

A multiple is in a number’s times table: 6, 12, 18, 24 … are multiples of 6. 4 is a factor of 12, and 12 is a multiple of 4.

A common factor divides two numbers. List the factors of each and find the ones in both lists.

Example

Find the common factors of 12 and 18.

Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18.

Answer: 1, 2, 3 and 6

Prime and composite numbers

A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. A composite number has more than two factors. 1 is neither. 2 is the only even prime.

Prime numbers up to 19 (learn these)
2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19

To check a number up to 100, try dividing by 2, 3, 5 and 7. If none of them works, it is prime.

Example

Is 51 prime?

5 + 1 = 6, so 51 divides by 3: 51 = 3 × 17.

Answer: No, 51 is composite

A prime factor is a factor that is prime. A factor tree splits a number until every branch ends in a prime.

Square numbers and cube numbers

A square number is a number multiplied by itself. We write 5² (5 squared) for 5 × 5 = 25.

A cube number is a number multiplied by itself three times. We write 3³ (3 cubed) for 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

Example

Work out 4³.

4 × 4 = 16, then 16 × 4 = 64.

Answer: 64

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Saying 1 is primeA prime has exactly two factors. 1 has only one
Saying 2 is not prime because it is even2 has two factors, 1 and 2. It is the only even prime
Thinking every odd number is prime: 51, 57, 9151 = 3 × 17, 57 = 3 × 19, 91 = 7 × 13
Missing a factor pairTest 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order until the pairs meet
Mixing up factors and multiples: 4 is a multiple of 124 is a factor of 12; 12 is a multiple of 4
7² = 147² = 7 × 7 = 49
3³ = 93³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27

faq.q: What are factors and multiples in Year 5?
faq.a: A factor divides a number exactly, and a multiple is in its times table. In Year 5 children find all the factor pairs of a number, multiples, and the common factors of two numbers.

faq.q: What prime numbers should Year 5 know?
faq.a: Year 5 pupils should recall the prime numbers up to 19 (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19) and be able to check whether any number up to 100 is prime.
No. A prime number has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one. 1 is neither prime nor composite, and the smallest prime number is 2.

faq.q: What do ² and ³ mean in maths?
faq.a: ² means squared, a number multiplied by itself: 7² = 7 × 7 = 49. ³ means cubed, a number multiplied by itself three times: 3³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.

sets.title: Factor pairs and all the factors

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 12?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Do not forget 1 and 12, and do not miss 3 × 4. 12, 24, 36, 48 are multiples of 12, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 20?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 20, 2 × 10, 4 × 5. So the factors are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Do not forget 1 and 20, and do not miss 4 × 5. 20, 40, 60, 80 are multiples of 20, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 24?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8, 4 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Do not forget 1 and 24, and do not miss 3 × 8. 24, 48, 72, 96 are multiples of 24, not factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the factors of 30?
items.e: Find the factor pairs: 1 × 30, 2 × 15, 3 × 10, 5 × 6. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. Do not forget 1 and 30, and do not miss 5 × 6. 30, 60, 90, 120 are multiples of 30, not factors.

items.q: This array shows 18 dots. Which factor pair of 18 does it show?
items.e: There are 3 rows of 6 dots: 3 × 6 = 18. So 3 × 6 is a factor pair of 18. 2 × 9 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 3 + 6 = 9, not 18.
There are 4 rows of 7 dots: 4 × 7 = 28. So 4 × 7 is a factor pair of 28. 2 × 14 is another pair, but it is not the one shown, and 4 + 7 = 11, not 28.

items.q: Which of these is a factor pair of 36?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a factor pair. 6 × 5 = 30, 3 × 13 = 39 and 2 × 16 = 32. The other pairs of 36 are 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12 and 6 × 6.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 24. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 3, so 3 × ? = 24. 24 ÷ 3 = 8. 21 is 24 − 3, not 24 ÷ 3. 9 and 7 are not factors of 24.

items.q: The factor rainbow shows all the factors of 30. Which number is missing?
items.e: The arc joins ? to 2, so 2 × ? = 30. 30 ÷ 2 = 15. 28 is 30 − 2, 60 is 30 × 2, and 10 is already in the rainbow (it pairs with 3).

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 32?
items.e: 32 ÷ 6 = 5 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 32. 4 × 8 = 32. 8 × 4 = 32. 16 × 2 = 32.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 45?
items.e: 45 ÷ 6 = 7 remainder 3, so 6 is not a factor of 45. 3 × 15 = 45. 9 × 5 = 45. 15 × 3 = 45.

items.q: Which number is not a factor of 56?
Which number is a factor of 42?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42, so 7 is a factor of 42. 84 is a multiple of 42, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: Which number is a factor of 54?
items.e: 9 × 6 = 54, so 9 is a factor of 54. 108 is a multiple of 54, not a factor, and 8 and 12 leave a remainder.

items.q: How many factors does 16 have?
items.e: The factor pairs are 1 × 16, 2 × 8 and 4 × 4. The factors are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16: 5 factors. 4 × 4 uses 4 only once, so do not count it twice (6). 3 is the number of pairs.

items.q: How many factor pairs does 24 have?
items.e: 1 × 24, 2 × 12, 3 × 8 and 4 × 6. That is 4 factor pairs. 8 is the number of factors, not pairs.

items.q: Leo lists the factor pairs of 48: 1 × 48, 2 × 24, 3 × 16, 6 × 8. Which pair did he miss?
items.e: Test 1, 2, 3, 4 … in order. 48 ÷ 4 = 12, so 4 × 12 is missing. 8 × 6 is the same pair as 6 × 8. 5 × 10 = 50 and 7 × 7 = 49, not 48.

items.q: Which number has exactly 3 factors?
items.e: The factors of 9 are 1, 3 and 9: 3 factors (3 × 3 counts 3 once). 6 has 4 factors (1, 2, 3, 6), 7 has 2 (1, 7), and 12 has 6.

items.q: Ethan says 7 is a factor of 27 because 27 has a 7 in it. Is he right?
items.e: 7 × 3 = 21 and 7 × 4 = 28, so 27 is not in the 7 times table. 27 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 6, so 7 is not a factor. The digits do not matter. 27 is not prime either: 27 = 3 × 9.

items.q: What is the largest factor of 35 that is less than 35?
items.e: The factors of 35 are 1, 5, 7 and 35. The largest one below 35 is 7. 34 is 35 − 1, and 35 ÷ 2 is not a whole number, so 17 is not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 6?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42, so 42 is a multiple of 6. 16 ÷ 6 = 2 remainder 4. 26 ÷ 6 = 4 remainder 2. 63 ÷ 6 = 10 remainder 3. Having a 6 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 6.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 8?
items.e: 8 × 9 = 72, so 72 is a multiple of 8. 28 ÷ 8 = 3 remainder 4. 18 ÷ 8 = 2 remainder 2. 84 ÷ 8 = 10 remainder 4. Having an 8 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 8.

items.q: Which number is a multiple of 9?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so 81 is a multiple of 9. 19 ÷ 9 = 2 remainder 1. 39 ÷ 9 = 4 remainder 3. 89 ÷ 9 = 9 remainder 8. Having a 9 as a digit does not make a number a multiple of 9.

items.q: Which number is not a multiple of 7?
items.e: 7 × 6 = 42 and 7 × 7 = 49, so 47 is not in the 7 times table. 7 × 7 = 49, 7 × 8 = 56 and 7 × 5 = 35.

items.q: What is the 6th multiple of 8?
items.e: The 6th multiple of 8 is 8 × 6 = 48. 40 is the 5th multiple, 56 is the 7th, and 14 is 8 + 6.

items.q: Which list shows the first five multiples of 4?
items.e: The multiples of 4 are 4 × 1, 4 × 2, 4 × 3 …: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. The first multiple is 4 itself. 1, 2, 4 are the factors of 4.

items.q: Arjun shades the multiples of 3 on this number track. Which multiple of 3 has he missed?
items.e: Count in 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18. 3 × 5 = 15 is not shaded. 13 has a 3 as a digit, but 13 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 1. 16 and 10 are not multiples of 3.

items.q: Freya says 30 is a factor of 5. Is she right?
items.e: 5 × 6 = 30, so 30 is a multiple of 5, and 5 is a factor of 30. A factor divides the number; a multiple is in its times table.

items.q: Which statement is true?
items.e: 7 × 8 = 56, so 7 is a factor of 56 (and 56 is a multiple of 7). 56 ÷ 6 = 9 remainder 2, so 6 is not a factor of 56.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 12 and 16?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 4. Remember 1, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 15 and 25?
items.e: Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. Factors of 25: 1, 5, 25. The numbers in both lists are 1, 5. Remember 1, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which list shows all the common factors of 18 and 24?
items.e: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The numbers in both lists are 1, 2, 3, 6. Remember 1, and use only numbers that divide both.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 20 and 30?
items.e: 5 × 4 = 20 and 5 × 6 = 30, so 5 is a common factor. 4 is a factor of 20 only, 3 is a factor of 30 only, and 60 is a multiple of both, not a factor.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 24 and 32?
items.e: 8 × 3 = 24 and 8 × 4 = 32, so 8 is a common factor. 3 is a factor of 24 only, 16 is a factor of 32 only, and 96 is a multiple of both, not a factor.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 36 and 48?
items.e: 9 is a factor of 36, but 48 ÷ 9 = 5 remainder 3, so 9 is not a common factor. 2, 4 and 12 divide both numbers.

items.q: Which number is not a common factor of 40 and 60?
items.e: 8 is a factor of 40, but 60 ÷ 8 = 7 remainder 4, so 8 is not a common factor. 4, 5 and 10 divide both numbers.

items.q: Which pair of numbers has only 1 as a common factor?
items.e: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. The only common factor is 1, so the answer is 9 and 14. 9 and 12 share 3, 8 and 14 share 2, and 10 and 15 share 5.

items.q: How many common factors do 12 and 18 have?
items.e: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. That is 4. Do not forget 1 (that gives 3). 6 is the largest common factor, not how many.

items.q: Poppy says 2 is a common factor of 10 and 15. Is she right?
c: Yes. Both are in the 5 times table
No. 2 is not a factor of 15
items.e: A common factor must divide both numbers. 2 divides 10, but 15 is odd, so 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1. 2 is not a common factor. The common factors of 10 and 15 are 1 and 5.

items.q: Which number is a common factor of 12, 18 and 30?
items.e: 6 × 2 = 12, 6 × 3 = 18 and 6 × 5 = 30, so 6 divides all three. 4 does not divide 18, 9 does not divide 12 or 30, and 12 does not divide 18 or 30.

sets.title: Prime numbers, composite numbers and prime factors

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 13 has exactly two factors, 1 and 13, so 13 is prime. 15 = 3 × 5, so 15 is not prime. 21 = 3 × 7, so 21 is not prime. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime.

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 29 has exactly two factors, 1 and 29, so 29 is prime. 27 = 3 × 9, so 27 is not prime. 39 = 3 × 13, so 39 is not prime. 49 = 7 × 7, so 49 is not prime.

items.q: Which of these is a prime number?
items.e: 17 has exactly two factors, 1 and 17, so 17 is prime. 51 = 3 × 17, so 51 is not prime. 9 = 3 × 3, so 9 is not prime. 57 = 3 × 19, so 57 is not prime.

items.q: Which number is not a prime number?
items.e: 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. 2, 3 and 5 are prime: each has exactly two factors. 2 is prime, even though it is even.

items.q: Which number is not a prime number?
items.e: 57 = 3 × 19, so 57 is not prime. 2, 59 and 43 are prime: each has exactly two factors. 2 is prime, even though it is even.

items.q: Which number is not a prime number?
items.e: 91 = 7 × 13, so 91 is not prime. 71, 97 and 61 are prime: each has exactly two factors.

items.q: Which list shows all the prime numbers up to 19?
items.e: The primes up to 19 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19. Learn them by heart. 1 is not prime, 2 is prime, 9 = 3 × 3 and 15 = 3 × 5 are not prime, and do not leave out 19.

items.q: Is 51 a prime number?
c: Yes. It has only two factors
items.e: Test small primes. 5 + 1 = 6, which is in the 3 times table, so 51 divides by 3: 51 = 3 × 17. So 51 is not prime. Being odd does not make a number prime, and 5 × 11 = 55.

items.q: Which number is composite?
items.e: A composite number has more than two factors. 39 = 3 × 13, so 39 is composite. 2 and 37 are prime. 1 is neither prime nor composite: it has only one factor.

items.q: How many factors does a prime number have?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 7 has factors 1 and 7. A number with more than two factors is composite.

items.q: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 30?
items.e: The odd numbers are 21, 23, 25, 27, 29. 21 = 3 × 7, 25 = 5 × 5 and 27 = 3 × 9, so only 23 and 29 are prime: 2 primes. Counting every odd number gives 5, and 3 or 4 means a number like 21, 25 or 27 was counted.

items.q: Grace says every odd number is prime. Which number shows she is wrong?
items.e: 15 is odd, but 15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime. 15 shows the rule is wrong. 13 and 11 are odd and prime, so they fit the rule, and 2 is not odd.

items.q: Evie says 2 is not a prime number because it is even. Is she right?
items.e: The factors of 2 are 1 and 2, so 2 is prime. It is the only even prime: every other even number divides by 2.

items.q: Harry says 1 is a prime number. Is he right?
items.e: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 1 has only one factor, so it is not prime. It is not composite either.

items.q: Which shows 12 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3. 3 × 4 is not finished, because 4 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 = 6, not 12.

items.q: Which shows 18 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 18 = 2 × 3 × 3. 3 × 6 is not finished, because 6 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 3 = 6, not 18.

items.q: Which shows 40 as a product of prime factors?
items.e: Keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime: 40 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 5. 5 × 8 is not finished, because 8 is not prime. 1 is not prime, so it is not written. 2 × 5 = 10, not 40.

items.q: What are the prime factors of 42?
items.e: 42 = 2 × 3 × 7, and 2, 3 and 7 are all prime. So the prime factors are 2, 3 and 7. 1 is not prime, 6 = 2 × 3 and 21 = 3 × 7.

items.q: Which number is a prime factor of 35?
items.e: 35 = 5 × 7, and 7 is prime, so 7 is a prime factor. 35 is a factor but not prime, 1 is not prime, and 3 is prime but not a factor of 35.

items.q: What is 2 × 2 × 3 × 5?
items.e: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 5 = 60. So the prime factors of 60 are 2, 2, 3 and 5. 12 comes from adding, 30 uses only one 2, and 120 uses three 2s.
There are 6 rows of 6 dots: 6 × 6 = 6² = 36. 36 is a square number. 12 is 6 + 6, 20 counts only the dots round the edge, and 25 is 5 × 5.

items.q: What is 7²?
items.e: 7² means 7 × 7 = 49. It does not mean 7 × 2 = 14 or 7 + 2 = 9. 343 is 7³.

items.q: What is 9²?
items.e: 9² means 9 × 9 = 81. It does not mean 9 × 2 = 18 or 9 + 2 = 11. 729 is 9³.

items.q: What is 3³?
What is 5³?
This cube is made of small cubes. How many small cubes are there?
items.e: It has 2 layers of 2 × 2 = 4 cubes: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = 8. 4 is only the top layer, and 7 counts only the cubes you can see: one is hidden at the back.
It has 3 layers of 3 × 3 = 9 cubes: 3 × 3 × 3 = 3³ = 27. 9 is one layer, 18 is two layers, and 19 counts only the cubes you can see.

items.q: Which of these is a square number?
items.e: 9 × 9 = 81, so 81 is a square number. 18 is 9 × 2, 27 is a cube number (3 × 3 × 3), and 90 is between 9 × 9 and 10 × 10.

items.q: Which of these is a square number?
items.e: 4 × 4 = 16, so 16 is a square number. 8 is a cube number (2 × 2 × 2), 12 is 4 × 3, and 32 is between 5 × 5 and 6 × 6.

items.q: Which of these is a cube number?
items.e: 4 × 4 × 4 = 16 × 4 = 64, so 64 is a cube number. 16 is 4², a square number, 12 is 4 × 3, and 36 is 6².

items.q: Which list shows the first five square numbers?
items.e: 1 × 1 = 1, 2 × 2 = 4, 3 × 3 = 9, 4 × 4 = 16, 5 × 5 = 25: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25. The first square number is 1. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 are multiples of 2, and 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 are cube numbers.

items.q: Which list shows the first four cube numbers?
Work out 4² + 3²
items.e: 4² = 16 and 3² = 9. 16 + 9 = 25. 14 comes from 4 × 2 + 3 × 2, and 49 from adding first: 7 × 7. 12 is 4 × 3.

items.q: Work out 2³ + 3²
Work out 6² − 5²
Which is greater, 3³ or 5²?
items.e: 3³ = 3 × 3 × 3 = 27 and 5² = 5 × 5 = 25. 27 is greater, so 3³ is greater. Using 3³ = 9 or 5² = 10 gives the wrong answer.

items.q: Which number is a square number between 50 and 70?
items.e: 7 × 7 = 49 is less than 50 and 9 × 9 = 81 is more than 70. 8 × 8 = 64. 56 is 7 × 8 and 63 is 7 × 9, not square numbers.

items.q: What is the 12th square number?
items.e: The 12th square number is 12² = 12 × 12 = 144. 24 is 12 × 2, 122 is 12 and 2 written side by side, and 121 is 11², the 11th square number.

items.q: Oliver says 8² = 16. Is he right?
items.e: The small 2 means multiply 8 by itself: 8 × 8 = 64. It does not mean 8 × 2 or 8 + 2. 512 is 8³ = 8 × 8 × 8.

items.q: Find the missing number: ?³ = 64
items.e: 4 × 4 × 4 = 16 × 4 = 64, so the missing number is 4. 8 × 8 = 64 is 8², not a cube. 21 comes from 64 ÷ 3, but cubed means multiply three times, not × 3. 16 is 4².

items.q: I am a square number between 30 and 40. What number am I?
items.e: 5 × 5 = 25 and 6 × 6 = 36 and 7 × 7 = 49. The only square number between 30 and 40 is 36. 49 is square but more than 40. 32 and 34 are not square numbers.

items.q: I am a prime number between 30 and 40. My digits add up to 4. What number am I?
items.e: The primes between 30 and 40 are 31 and 37. 3 + 1 = 4, so the number is 31. 13 has digits that add to 4, but it is not between 30 and 40. 39 = 3 × 13 is not prime.

items.q: I am a cube number between 50 and 100. What number am I?
items.e: 3³ = 27, 4³ = 64 and 5³ = 125. So the cube number between 50 and 100 is 64. 81 is a square number (9 × 9), and 125 is more than 100.

items.q: A teacher puts 36 chairs in equal rows, with none left over. Which could not be the number of chairs in each row?
items.e: The number in each row must be a factor of 36. 36 ÷ 8 = 4 remainder 4, so 8 chairs does not work. 4 × 9 = 36 and 6 × 6 = 36.

items.q: The hall has 30 chairs for a school assembly. Which layout uses all 30 chairs in equal rows?
Kai has 17 counters. Can he put them all in a rectangle with more than one row and the same number in each row?
items.e: 17 is prime: its only factors are 1 and 17, so the only rectangle is 1 row of 17. 2 × 8 = 16 and 3 × 6 = 18. Being odd is not the reason: 15 is odd and makes 3 rows of 5.

items.q: Packets of crisps come in multipacks of 6. Which number of packets can you buy exactly?
items.e: You can only buy a multiple of 6. 6 × 8 = 48. 26 and 16 have a 6 as a digit but are not multiples of 6, and 40 ÷ 6 = 6 remainder 4.

items.q: Biscuits come in packets of 8. Ava needs at least 30 biscuits for her class. What is the fewest packets she can buy?
items.e: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32. 3 packets give 24, which is not enough. 4 packets give 32. 5 packets give 40, which is more than needed.

items.q: Aisha has 12 red beads and 18 blue beads. She makes bracelets that are all the same, using every bead. How many bracelets could she make?
items.e: The number of bracelets must be a common factor of 12 and 18. 6 works: each bracelet has 2 red and 3 blue beads, so 6 bracelets. 4 divides 12 but not 18, 9 divides 18 but not 12, and 36 is a multiple, not a factor.

items.q: A baker has 20 cupcakes and 30 biscuits. She packs them into boxes that are all the same, with none left over. How many boxes could she use?
items.e: The number of boxes must divide 20 and 30. 20 ÷ 10 = 2 and 30 ÷ 10 = 3, so 10 boxes work. 4 divides 20 but not 30, 6 divides 30 but not 20, and 60 is a multiple of both.

items.q: A class has fewer than 40 pupils. They can line up in 2s, 3s or 5s with no one left over. How many pupils are in the class?
items.e: The number must be a multiple of 2, 3 and 5. 2 × 3 × 5 = 30. 10 is not a multiple of 3, and 15 and 35 are odd, so they are not multiples of 2.

items.q: Isla is older than 5 and younger than 15. Her age is a prime number. Next year her age will be a multiple of 6. How old is she?
items.e: The primes from 6 to 14 are 7, 11 and 13. Next year they become 8, 12 and 14. Only 12 is a multiple of 6, so she is 11. 12 is next year’s age, 13 + 1 = 14 is not a multiple of 6, and 5 is too young.

items.q: A square patio is made of 49 square tiles. How many tiles are along each side?
items.e: A square has the same number of tiles along each side. 7 × 7 = 49, so there are 7 tiles. 14 comes from 7 × 2, 12 from 49 ÷ 4, and 9 × 9 = 81.

items.q: A big cube is built from small cubes, with 4 small cubes along each edge. How many small cubes are used?
items.e: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 16 × 4 = 64. 16 is one layer (4 × 4), 12 is 4 × 3, and 48 is only 3 layers.

items.q: Noah has 100 small cubes. He builds the biggest solid cube he can. How many small cubes does he use?
items.e: Cube numbers: 27, 64, 125. 125 is more than 100, so the biggest cube uses 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cubes. 100 is a square number, not a cube, and 81 is 9 × 9.

items.q: Ruby thinks of a number between 10 and 30. It is a multiple of 4 and a factor of 40. What is her number?
items.e: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Between 10 and 30 there is only 20, and 20 = 4 × 5, so the number is 20. 12 and 24 are multiples of 4 but not factors of 40, and 10 is not a multiple of 4.

items.q: Maya says all prime numbers are odd. Which number shows she is wrong?
items.e: 2 is prime (its factors are 1 and 2), and it is even. 9 and 15 are odd numbers that are not prime, and 1 is not prime, so none of them shows the rule is wrong.

items.q: Two prime numbers add up to 20. Their difference is 6. What are they?
items.e: 7 + 13 = 20 and 13 − 7 = 6, and both are prime: 7 and 13. 3 and 17 are prime but differ by 14. 1 is not prime, and 9 = 3 × 3 is not prime.

items.q: 28 pupils split into equal groups. Each group has more than 1 and fewer than 10 pupils. How many different group sizes are possible?
items.e: The group size must be a factor of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. Between 1 and 10 that leaves 2, 4 and 7: 3 sizes. 6 counts every factor, and 4 wrongly includes 14.

items.q: I am a two-digit number. I am a square number and also a cube number. What number am I?
items.e: 64 = 8 × 8 and 64 = 4 × 4 × 4, so 64 is both. 16 and 81 are only square numbers, and 27 = 3 × 3 × 3 is only a cube number.
